title: Lebesgue measure is at most (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d] on ℝ^d (completion of Simon 2.9)
statement: For every d ∈ ℕ, the Lebesgue measure L^d = volume on ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is dominated by (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d]: L^d(s) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d](s) for every set s ⊆ ℝ^d (as measures, L^d ≤ (ω_d/2^d)•μH[d]). Here ω_d = unitBallVolume d = L^d(ball(0, 1)), and μH[d] is Mathlib's d-dimensional Hausdorff measure (weight diam^d, no normalising constant).
lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ), (volume : Measure (Euclid d)) ≤ (unitBallVolume d / 2 ^ d) • (μH[(d : ℝ)] : Measure (Euclid d))
